en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (5) 17.20.
Kusala-ttika, Sanidassana-ttika

An indeterminate (abyākata) phenomenon that is visible and impinging (sanidassana-sappaṭigha) is not a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), for an indeterminate phenomenon that is neither visible nor impinging (na-sanidassana-na-sappaṭigha). (Three [combinations] should be understood; they are to be formulated.

There are six [conditions] in the case of the object, three in the case of predominance (adhipati), and six in the cases of decisive support (upanissaya), prenascence (purejāta), presence (atthi), and non-disappearance (avigata).
In dependence on an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible but impinging (anidassana-sappaṭigha), a wholesome (kusala) phenomenon that is neither invisible nor impinging arises.

[It] arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on an indeterminate (*abyākata*), non-demonstrable (*anidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*) phenomenon, an unwholesome (*naakusala*) and non-demonstrable-impinging phenomenon arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate, non-demonstrable, and impinging phenomenon, [there arise] both a non-wholesome and non-demonstrable-impinging phenomenon and an unwholesome and non-demonstrable-impinging phenomenon...
And states arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Three in the case of the root;
three in the case of the predominance ... pe ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor non-demonstrable and non-reactive.

[It] arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome (kusala) invisible-non-reactive (anidassana-appaṭigha) state, an unwholesome (na-akusala) invisible-non-reactive state arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome invisible-non-reactive state, both a non-wholesome non-invisible-non-reactive state and a non-unwholesome non-invisible-non-reactive state arise by way of root condition. ... [Three.]
Dependent on an unwholesome, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor non-demonstrable and non-reactive, by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, there arises a state that is not wholesome and not non-demonstrable and non-reactive, by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, there arises a state that is not wholesome...
Neither-unseen-nor-reacting and unwholesome states, and neither-unseen-nor-reacting states, arise with a root condition... three.
Dependent on an indeterminate, neither-unseen-nor-reacting state, an unwholesome, neither-unseen-nor-reacting state arises with a root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, neither-unseen-nor-reacting state, a neither-unwholesome-nor-indeterminate, neither-unseen-nor-reacting [state] arises with a root condition.

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor indeterminate, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive, by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on a wholesome, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, and an indeterminate, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor indeterminate, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive, by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on unwholesome and non-demonstrative-non-reactive states, and dependent on indeterminate and non-demonstrative-non-reactive states, a state that is neither wholesome nor non-demonstrative-non-reactive arises by way of root-condition. ... [Three] (Abbreviated). In the case of root, there are fifteen;
in the case of predominance, fifteen ... pe ... in the case of mutuality, three ... pe ... in the case of result, three ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, fifteen.
